finding: An operator who runs premerge-check from a subfolder of the repository gets two wrong lines: BLOCK code-review says no report exists, and PASS open-findings says no blocking finding is open, although both files are at the head. files_at_head calls `git ls-tree -r --name-only <branch> -- docs/reviews/`, and git ls-tree reads the path relative to the current folder, so from packages/ it lists packages/docs/reviews/. The review checked this in a scratch repository with a report and an open BUG-0091 at the head. The overall exit stays 1, because the review check fails closed, so no branch merges by mistake. merge-story runs premerge-check from the project root and is not affected. The behavior looks unintended. The smallest fix is to add --full-tree to the ls-tree call in files_at_head.
why_this_severity: The refusal still holds and merge-story always runs from the root (no to fails_purpose). An operator who runs the check by hand from a subfolder searches for a report that exists and misses a finding that is open.
